contentHtml:
It’s week two of June, and the AI world just did what it does best—be everywhere at once. From OpenAI quietly rolling out smarter memory in ChatGPT, to huge insurance companies letting AI fully handle crash claims, it’s clear the “agentic” era isn’t a buzzword anymore. But as everyday tools get more personal and powerful, the rules of who controls, benefits from, and profits off AI are shifting—sometimes in surprising ways.

TOP STORIES

ChatGPT Gets a Major Memory Upgrade to Personalize Conversations

  • OpenAI is rolling out a more scalable “memory” system for ChatGPT, designed to better remember user preferences and conversations across hundreds of millions of users.
  • This feature means ChatGPT will be more helpful and less forgetful—tracking your projects, correcting stale info, and scaling to long-term use.
  • The new memory system will become available to more users in stages, with enterprise access prioritized.
  • Source

S&P 500 Rejects SpaceX, Also Bars OpenAI and Anthropic From Index Entry

  • The S&P 500 stock market index denied SpaceX’s fast-track request for inclusion; the decision also blocks other unprofitable AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic from joining.
  • Analysts say S&P’s refusal signals a hard line against “growth-at-all-costs” firms—even if they dominate headlines and investment.
  • For regular investors, it means you won’t see OpenAI or Anthropic shares in your basic index funds anytime soon.
  • Source

OpenAI’s New GPT-Rosalind Update Aims at Real-World Science and Drug Discovery

  • OpenAI released an upgrade for GPT-Rosalind, its AI model tailored for life sciences, now powered by GPT-5.5 and able to run sophisticated “agent” workflows common in drug research.
  • The update brings better scientific reasoning and stronger tool integration for industry teams working on discovery pipelines.
  • Available now to enterprise customers; expect to see more biotech and pharma using AI for real, results-driven work.
  • Source

AI-Powered Claims Handling Now Covers Most U.S. Car Accidents at Travelers Insurance

  • Travelers, a major U.S. insurer, now resolves over 90% of accident claims via an “AI Claim Assistant” built with OpenAI tech.
  • Customers who call after a crash can have their claim filed and completed (often in real-time) by AI, even in disaster-level events.
  • This rollout is nationwide and signals how routine, high-volume tasks in big industries are quietly going fully AI-driven.
  • Source

Endava Moves Its Entire Software Delivery Pipeline to AI Agents

  • Endava, a global tech consultancy, announced it’s redesigning how it delivers software—putting AI agents at the center of workflows from project kickoff to code deployment.
  • For clients, this means faster releases, fewer handoffs, and more dynamic updates—but also big shifts in job roles and required skills.
  • Early adopters can expect a blend of automation and human oversight; broader rollouts are coming in months.
  • Source

Wasmer Uses OpenAI Codex to Make Node.js Apps Run Securely “at the Edge”

  • Wasmer engineers used Codex and GPT-5.5 to develop a new way to run Node.js (JavaScript) apps, agents, and microservices inside a secure sandboxed WebAssembly environment.
  • This approach claims to speed up developer work by 10–20x, opening up secure, scalable web applications that can deploy anywhere—from cloud to your laptop.
  • It’s a sign of AI lowering barriers for complex tech projects, making next-gen apps more accessible to smaller teams.
  • Source

THIS WEEK IN AI

What’s more personal than memory? This week, OpenAI decided it was time to tackle one of AI’s most persistent annoyances: the fact that your AI assistant didn’t remember you. Rolling out a scalable, non-forgetful “memory” for ChatGPT is a deceptively simple update. But for millions of us who use ChatGPT as a work tool, sidekick, or substitute for tedious admin, this changes the game. The AI that knows your context, remembers your last request, and gets smarter the more it helps—you might wonder: is this the beginning of real AI companionship, or just the next level of digital lock-in?

Alongside this, we’re seeing a massive expansion of AI’s reach into “serious” industries. There’s something quietly radical about 90% of Travelers’ accident claims now routed through an AI agent. Not only does it mean faster resolutions (and likely cost cuts for insurers), it’s a signal to all of us: if you thought AI was just parlor tricks or novelty text generators, you’re missing the real story. The boring, repetitive work that makes giant businesses tick is being handed off to technology—efficient, tireless, and, for now, not looking for a promotion.

But it wouldn’t be a week in AI without reminders that there are boundaries still being enforced. The S&P 500’s curt “no” to SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic’s index inclusion is a statement: profits still matter, and financial gatekeepers won’t cave to hype or vision alone. It raises hard questions—should the public be able to own a piece of these transformative (but risky) AI labs? Are Wall Street rules holding back progress, or preventing disaster?

The “agentic” trend, meanwhile, is seeping into every workflow imaginable—from Endava’s code factories to the biotech labs harnessing GPT-Rosalind for drug research. Every organization trying to move faster is essentially building itself around machines that act on their own, updating their memory and context with every task. But how do we deal with the friction this introduces for human workers? If AI can handle more context than a person ever could, where does that leave skills and careers that once seemed future-proof?

Here’s the challenge for all of us: Next time you use ChatGPT, actually switch on and try the new memory features. What part of your work or routine would genuinely be better if the AI just “knew” you and didn’t start from scratch every time? And when you see another headline about AI handling thousands of tasks per minute, ask yourself—are you watching from the sidelines, or are you learning how to direct these new agents yourself?

MORE TOP STORIES

OpenAI Releases Its First Public Policy Agenda, Vows to Democratize AI

  • OpenAI published a detailed policy playbook describing how AI should benefit everyone, not just tech giants or a select few.
  • Its five core principles emphasize resisting power concentration and ensuring user empowerment, aiming for inclusive global impact.
  • The document signals how major labs hope to shape regulation—and public expectations—as AI gets more capable.
  • Source

New “Democratic Governance” Blueprint for Frontier AI Released

  • OpenAI detailed proposals for a U.S. federal approach to governing dangerous or advanced AI, outlining a three-part plan to align oversight.
  • The blueprint addresses legal, technical, and institutional tools for handling the next generation of AI systems.
  • It’s an attempt by industry to influence how potentially risky models are managed before government moves too slowly.
  • Source

AI Overtakes Coding: 80% of New Wasmer Node.js Runtime Built With GPT-5.5 Codex

  • The Wasmer project leveraged OpenAI tools to rapidly develop a complex, secure runtime for JavaScript apps on the web’s “edge.”
  • They claim development speed increased by up to 20x, showing how agentic AI now shapes complex software, not just text output.
  • Such advances make it easier for small teams to build and deploy next-gen applications previously only possible for giants.
  • Source

Codex Now Used by Over 5 Million People Beyond Programmers

  • OpenAI released new data showing its Codex tool, initially built for coding, has spread as a general productivity booster.
  • More than 5 million people use Codex weekly to automate routine tasks across many fields, not just software development.
  • The expansion points to AI assistants moving from specialist tools into daily business and knowledge work.
  • Source

Google I/O Used Gemini Agents to Build Its Own Conference

  • Google revealed that the flagship I/O 2026 developer event was itself largely “built by AI,” with Gemini models and agents doing everything from presentations to logistics.
  • The company’s meta-move signals that AI agent workflows aren’t just demo material—they’re production-ready, even for high-profile events.
  • Expect accelerated adoption across events, marketing, and operations in other major organizations.
  • Source

Holo3.1 Launches Fast, Local Computer-Use Agents for Cloud and Device

  • The Holo3.1 agent family lets users run “digital worker” tasks across desktop, mobile, or cloud—claiming seamless switching between environments.
  • It boosts speed and privacy by supporting fully local execution on personal devices (not just cloud processing).
  • Available now via Hugging Face, this tech is a glimpse at where “your AI assistant” could actually live.
  • Source
